description: A plain `create index` (without CONCURRENTLY) on public.reviews takes a lock that blocks writes to that table for the duration of the index build. Whether this is actually a problem depends entirely on how large reviews currently is and how much concurrent write traffic hits it in production — neither of which this one-line migration shows.

optional_findings.justification: A plain CREATE INDEX holds a lock that blocks concurrent writes to public.reviews for as long as the index build takes. On a small or lightly-written table this is a total non-issue (near-instant); on a large, high-write-volume production table it can cause a noticeable write-blocking pause. This fixture shows neither the table's current size nor its write traffic, so the correct answer is that it CANNOT be confirmed from what's shown — not a confident assertion that this migration is unsafe.

explanation: Mirrors the code/security benchmarks' own ambiguous-fixture pattern (a plausible defect whose confirmation depends on production context not included in the diff): the three fully correct responses are (a) zero findings, (b) an explicit needs-more-context signal, or (c) a single low-confidence finding matching opt-1 suggesting CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY as a defensive default. A confident/high-confidence finding asserting this migration WILL cause an outage is an overclaim — reviews's actual current size is exactly the kind of unseen context the task instructions warn against assuming.
